work.title: Plato, Phaedo
work.notes: Plato's narrated dialogue about Socrates' final day. Its developed metaphysics of soul and Forms may reflect Plato's philosophy and must not be treated as a transparent transcript of the historical Socrates.

edition.label: Henry Cary English translation with Edward Brooks introduction; Project Gutenberg #13726
edition.licenseNote: Project Gutenberg metadata states public domain in the USA; verify the law of the deployment jurisdiction before production redistribution. The digitization visibly corrupts Phaedo's title as Ph?do and should be proofread before activation.

passages.translationText: "In reality, then, Simmias," he continued, "those who pursue philosophy rightly, study to die; and to them, of all men, death is least formidable.
passages.interpretiveNote: This alternative translation is archived for comparison but remains draft because the supplied digitization contains visible encoding and transcription defects. The passage must never be read as encouragement of self-harm.
passages.period: Platonic representation; error-prone historical English digitization
